parole.significato: Pertaining to a group of peoples mostly inhabiting Alaska, western Canada, the Pacific coast of California and Oregon,…
parole.testo: From Athabasca + -an, from Cree Ahđapaskâw (literally “where there are plants distributed in a net-like pattern”).

parole.significato: A Canadian porcupine (Erethizon dorsatum).
parole.testo: From Cree kâkwa / ᑳᑲᐧ (kaakay, “porcupine”).

parole.significato: grandmother (among the Cree people)
parole.testo: From Cree [Term?].

parole.significato: A white man.
parole.testo: From Cree.

parole.significato: The Moose Cree people.
parole.testo: From Cree ᒨᓱᓂᔾ (moosoniy).

parole.significato: A terrain composed of peat bog with tussocky meadow and woody vegetation including spruce.
parole.testo: From Cree ᒪᐢᑫᐠ (maskek).

parole.significato: The togue: a large North American lake trout, Salvelinus namaycush, usually spotted with red.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Cree ᓇᒣᑯᐢ (namekos, “lake trout”), from Proto-Algonquian *name·kwa (“lake trout”).

parole.significato: A food made from meat which has been dried and beaten into a paste, mixed with berries and rendered fat, and shaped int…
parole.testo: From Cree ᐱᒦᐦᑳᐣ (pimiihkaan, “pemmican”), from Cree ᐱᒥᕀ (pimiy, “grease, oil, lard”) + -ᐃᐦᑳᐣ (-ihkaan, “hand made”), from Proto-Algonquian *pemyi.

parole.significato: Any of several evergreen plants, of the genus Chimaphila of prince's pines
parole.testo: Perhaps from Cree [script needed] (pipsissewa, “breaks (stones in the body) into small pieces”) (compare ᐲᐏᓷᐤ (piiwiswew, “he or she cuts pieces off someone”)), or perhaps from Abenaki [Term?] (kpipskwáhsawe, “flower of the woods”).

parole.significato: The wolverine.
parole.testo: From East Cree *ᑸᐦᑾᐦᐋᒉᐤ (*kwiihkwahaacew) (modern Cree ᑮᐦᑿᐦᐋᐦᑫᐤ (kiihkwahaahkew, “wolverine”); compare Ojibwe gwiingwa'aage); assimilated to quick + hatch, omitting the middle syllable present in older forms.

parole.significato: A shrub inhabiting western North America (Amelanchier alnifolia).
parole.testo: From Cree ᒥᓵᐢᑿᑑᒥᐣ (misaaskwatoomin, “saskatoon berry”), from ᒥᓵᐢᑿᐟ (misaaskwat, “saskatoon shrub”) + ᒥᐣ (min, “berry”).

parole.significato: Amelanchier alnifolia, a shrub with edible berry-like fruit.
parole.testo: From Cree ᒥᓵᐢᐠᐘᑑᒥᓇ (misaaskwatoomina).

parole.significato: A rawhide strap, e.g. as used to hold together Red River carts.
parole.testo: From Cree ᐲᓵᑲᓈᐱᕀ (piisaakanaapiy, “rawhide thong, rope”) or a related word.

parole.significato: A whitefish (Coregonus artedi tullibee, formerly Coregonus tullibee) found in the Great Lakes of North America.
parole.testo: Perhaps from Cree *otonabi (“water mouth”) or Ojibwe odoonibii (“water mouth”).

parole.significato: The snow goose (Chen caerulescens)
parole.testo: According to one theory, from Cree. An alternative etymology, perhaps a folk etymology, attributes the name to their peculiar, wavy flight.

parole.significato: A fisher, Pekania pennanti, syn. Martes pennanti.
parole.testo: From Cree ocêk, otchek (“fisher”) or Ojibwe ojiig (“fisher, marten”). Doublet of woodchuck and woodshock.

parole.significato: Among the Cree, a non-Native American person; a white man.
parole.testo: From Cree, literally "he has a wooden boat", from ᒥᐢᑎᑯᓯ (mistikosi)/mistikosi (“wooden boat”).

parole.significato: The gray jay, Perisoreus canadensis.
parole.testo: Perhaps an alteration of whisky john, a corruption of Cree wîskacân / ᐄᐧᐢᑲᒑᐣ (iiyskacaan), or perhaps directly from Cree wîskicâk ᐄᐧᐢᑭᒑᐠ (iiyskicaak). See also Wisakedjak on Wikipedia.Wikipedia

parole.significato: A rodent of the family Sciuridae, belonging to the group of large ground squirrels known as marmots, Marmota monax.
parole.testo: Folk-etymological adaption of Cree ocêk, otchek (“fisher”), Ojibwe ojiig (“fisher, marten”), or a similar term in a related Algonquian language, subsequently reapplied to the groundhog. An earlier form of this word, woodshock, still sometimes designates the marten. Also a doublet of wejack.

parole.significato: The marten, or its pelt.
parole.testo: From the same Cree term ocêk, otchek (“fisher, marten”) or Ojibwe term ojiig (“fisher, marten”) which was taken into English as wejack in reference to the marten and as woodchuck in erroneous reference to the groundhog. Woodchuck may derive from woodshock.

parole.significato: A member of this people.
parole.testo: From a phonetic rendering of Canadian French Cris, short for Christinaux, from either Algonquin Kirishtinó, or Cree Kenisteniwuik.
